correctness.rationale: For fixed pair of orbital directions u1,u2 with dot product cosΔ, random inclination and initial phase are equivalent to a uniform line-of-sight vector. Failure at each visit is the disjoint antipodal cap pair |l·ui|>h, h=√(1−τ²). Pairwise intersections of signed caps have center separations δ and π−δ, yielding missed fraction [L(δ)+L(π−δ)]/(2π). Spherical excess yields L(s)=2π−4hβ−2γ on 0<s<2asinτ, and direct differentiation gives L′(s)=−2√(1−h²/cos²(s/2)), vanishing at tangency. Its strictly decreasing magnitude makes the probability monotone with the stated plateau for τ<1/√2 and unique quarter-orbit optimum otherwise. The rank-two sum of projectors ui ui^T has largest eigenvalue 1+|cosΔ|, attained at a signed bisector, proving the worst-case separation a√((1−|cosΔ|)/2). The tangent-cap overlap integral behaves as 4ε^{3/2}/3 with ε≈2√2(τ−τc), yielding the claimed constant. Independently integrated the physical detection event over 900,000 spherical test directions for five cases and verified the cap formula/maximum grids.
residual_risks: The detector model has only a single inner-working-angle separation cutoff: atmospheric brightness, outer-working angles and real visit costs are excluded.
Spherical grid is numerical corroboration, not continuum proof.

originality.rationale: Repeated-visit direct-imaging completeness and probability calculation are classical. Brown–Soummer define accumulated/dynamic completeness and Monte Carlo orbital sampling; Stark and others numerically optimize revisit timing with richer constraints. In accessible texts those methods do not state a closed two-visit all-threshold lens formula, full optimizer plateau, sharp all-orientation guarantee or 3/2 onset. The claim is therefore only the exact idealized special-case theorem, not a new generic imaging algorithm or realistic mission optimum.
residual_risks: A special-case quarter-orbit spherical-cap calculation may appear as an example or appendix in earlier exoplanet methodology not retrieved in full.
The physical model is intentionally idealized; realistic observability can break the optimizer.

value.rationale: The exact two-visit probability/guarantee question is a natural baseline for instrument scheduling when the orbit period/radius and geometric IWA are fixed. It distinguishes a whole interval of certain-detection spacings from a unique quarter-period optimum and quantifies the sharp 3/2 onset of unavoidable misses. The exact result is useful for unit-testing richer numerical completeness simulators, without claiming to optimize operational missions.
residual_risks: Does not cover planet contrast/phase or finite observation schedules beyond two instantaneous visits.

limitations: Isotropic random orientation and phase, circular orbit, fixed known period/radius, separation-only cutoff, exactly two visits.
Prior computational completeness literature extensively covers the physical setting.
